newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-NIGERIA SPLITS SQUAD TO LOOK AT FOREIGN-BASED PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NIGERIA SPLITS SQUAD TO LOOK AT FOREIGN-BASED PLAYERS.

text.p: Olympic champions Nigeria will select two entirely different teams for their next two international matches in order to have a closer look at their foreign-based players.

Nigeria, whose best players are scattered throughout the European leagues, face Turkey in Istanbul in a friendly on October 29, 11 days before a World Cup qualifying match against fellow West Africans Burkina Faso in Lagos.

"We decided to draw up two different squads for the two games to enable us to evaluate the current form of some players since we have so many good professionals abroad," coach Amodu Shaibu said on Thursday.
"It puts us in some difficulty of getting the best for both games but we believe it's the best thing to do in the circumstances."
Shaibu will manage the side for the World Cup qualifier while Olympic team coach Willy Bazuaye will take the other team to Turkey.
The bulk of both sides will be drawn from the Under-23 squad which beat Brazil and Argentina on their way to Olympic gold in Atlanta this August.
The decision to split the squad follows weeks of speculation about the future of Dutchman Jo Bonfrere, who was awarded a two-month holiday by the government for training the Olympic team to success.
Newspaper reports say Bonfrere has taken up a coaching job in Qatar and has no intention of returning to Nigeria.
"We decided to reorganise at the top as Bonfrere has remained incommunicado," Nigeria Football Association press officer Austin Mgbolu said. "But he has a deadline of October 28 to return."
